subject: opencode
title: LLM-generated command-arity dictionary collapses shell commands into human-scoped approval patterns
evidence: packages/opencode/src/permission/arity.ts:12-46 (generation prompt preserved in source; ARITY map git->2, "npm run"->3)
one_why: Makes 'always allow npm install' approvals actually mean npm install and nothing else, without a parser dependency; dictionary is regenerable and unit-tested (test/permission/arity.test.ts).

subject: opencode
title: CI gate proves every public HTTP route has a decode/auth/mutation scenario
one_why: Route coverage as a hard CI artifact (a missing scenario fails the build) is stronger than API test existence and maps directly onto our own agent HTTP surfaces.

subject: opencode
title: Confined tree-walking JS interpreter as one orchestration tool over the MCP catalog, promise-valued tool calls
one_why: Second shipping code-mode found in study (after codex v8) but TS-native and MCP-scoped: the model writes one script whose awaited expressions are tool calls, collapsing N round-trips into 1.

subject: opencode
title: Doom-loop detection re-enters as a permission ask instead of hard-stopping
evidence: packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:356-373 (3 identical tool calls -> permission.ask "doom_loop"); default-ask asserted test/agent/agent.test.ts:469-475
one_why: Unlike crush's breaker (hard abort), the user can wave the loop through once - breaker and steering unified through the same permission channel.

subject: opencode
title: Tree-sitter bash/ps parse extracts touched directories and arity-scoped patterns for per-command approval
one_why: Approval prompts know which outside-worktree directories a compound command touches before it runs - grammar beats regex denylists (our seeded anti-pattern) for scoping.

subject: opencode
title: Subagent sessions structurally cannot shed parent denies; task/todowrite denied unless the subagent's own ruleset grants them
evidence: packages/opencode/src/agent/subagent-permissions.ts:15-30; depth cap tool/task.ts:106-114; negative test test/permission-task.test.ts:87
one_why: Non-escalation is enforced by ruleset construction (deny-filter carried into child), not by trusting the spawned agent's config - clean default-deny nesting for fan-out workloads.

subject: opencode
title: Two session engines ship simultaneously with bidirectional bridge imports
evidence: V1 loop wired to HTTP route: server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/session.ts:11; V2 runner+coordinator wired into same server graph: httpapi/server.ts:301; V1 reads core/session/sql while core hosts core/src/v1/ and src/event-v2-bridge.ts
one_why: Every review question ('which loop is real?') now needs a path declaration; storage is shared but turn semantics are duplicated until V2 cuts over - the cost of shipping a rewrite in the open.

subject: opencode
title: Scripted SSE TestLLMServer plus recorded native-provider replay tests
one_why: Convergence datapoint (9th in study): scripted SSE drives loop semantics in CI, recorded replays catch provider wire drift - the pair, not either alone.

subject: opencode
title: SECURITY.md states the permission system is a UX feature, not isolation, with an explicit escape table
evidence: SECURITY.md:15-17 ("OpenCode does not sandbox the agent"), :30 (sandbox-escapes row)
one_why: Convergence datapoint for the calibration rule that an honest no-sandbox subject may score safety 6: opencode's candor matches pi's, its enforcement (grammar-scoped asks, deny-inheriting subagents) exceeds pi's.
